translations.text: What does it mean when carrot seeds fail to sprout

When carrot seeds sown in soil fail to emerge for an extended period or seedlings gradually or suddenly die back, it is usually a combination of unfavorable environmental conditions in the soil crust that is responsible. Carrots have very small seeds, and shallow planting depth combined with high sensitivity to cold soil, surface drying, and crusting causes germination failure in many gardens
In the source region, carrot seed planting is considered permissible only after soil temperature has reached a minimum of 40 °F; below this threshold, growth does not begin
. Optimal germination temperature is reported between 55 and 65 °F, and within this range, emergence takes approximately 14 to 21 days

When the soil surface seals and hardens after irrigation or rain, carrot seedlings, due to their small size and limited energy, are unable to penetrate the crust. In this case, emergence is restricted and plant structure is damaged
